source.text: וָאָשֻׁ֗ב וָאֶשָּׂ֤א עֵינַי֙ וָֽאֶרְאֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה אַרְבַּ֤ע מַרְכָּבוֹת֙ יֹֽצְא֔וֹת מִבֵּ֖ין שְׁנֵ֣י הֶֽהָרִ֑ים וְהֶהָרִ֖ים הָרֵ֥י נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And I returned and lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, four chariots coming out from between the two mountains; and the mountains [were] mountains of bronze.

en.L: And again I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, four chariots coming out from between the two mountains; and the mountains [were] mountains of bronze.
en.B: Again I looked up, and I saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains were made of bronze.
en.R: I looked up again and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains. The mountains were made of bronze.

decisions.choice: the eighth vision: four chariots sent out through the earth
decisions.reason: The last vision answers the first. In 1:8-11 horsemen patrolled the earth and found it at rest while Jerusalem lay in ruins. Here four chariots, drawn by horses of different colors, go out from the LORD's presence to the four quarters, and the one sent north brings the LORD's spirit to rest there (verse 8). The angel explains them as the four winds of heaven (verse 5).

decisions.choice: the two mountains of bronze: the gateway from the LORD's presence
alternatives: the two bronze pillars of the temple
decisions.reason: The text does not explain the mountains. The article, "the two mountains", suggests a place the hearer would know. The chariots come out from standing before the Lord of all the earth (verse 5), so the mountains seem to mark the entrance to his presence. Bronze suggests strength that cannot be broken. Some see a likeness to the two bronze pillars at the entrance of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 7:15-22), or to mountains where, in other ancient writings, the sun was pictured rising between two peaks.

decisions.choice: chariots: war chariots, the strongest force of an ancient army
decisions.reason: Horse-drawn chariots were the power of kings (Exodus 14:7; 1 Kings 10:26). Elisha's servant saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire around them (2 Kings 6:17). The chariots here are the LORD's forces, sent out to carry out his will.

decisions.choice: Again I looked up (B); I looked up again (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:1, Balanced and Readable say "looked up" for "lifted up my eyes".

source.text: בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֥ה הָרִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה סוּסִ֣ים אֲדֻמִּ֑ים וּבַמֶּרְכָּבָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית סוּסִ֥ים שְׁחֹרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: With the chariot the first [were] horses red, and with the chariot the second horses black,

en.L: With the first chariot [were] red horses, and with the second chariot black horses,
en.B: The first chariot had red horses, the second black horses,
en.R: Red horses pulled the first chariot, and black horses pulled the second.

decisions.choice: the colors of the horses: not explained
decisions.reason: The angel explains where the chariots go (verses 6-8), but not what the colors mean, as in the first vision (1:8). The red horses are not mentioned again. Revelation 6:1-8 takes up horses of these colors for its four riders.

decisions.choice: Red horses pulled the first chariot (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says how the horses went with the chariots and ends the sentence here; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew sentence, which runs into verse 3, and end with a comma.

source.text: וּבַמֶּרְכָּבָ֥ה הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֖ית סוּסִ֣ים לְבָנִ֑ים וּבַמֶּרְכָּבָה֙ הָרְבִעִ֔ית סוּסִ֥ים בְּרֻדִּ֖ים אֲמֻצִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and with the chariot the third horses white, and with the chariot the fourth horses dappled, strong.

en.L: and with the third chariot white horses, and with the fourth chariot dappled horses, strong ones.
en.B: the third white horses, and the fourth dappled horses, powerful ones.
en.R: White horses pulled the third chariot, and strong, spotted horses pulled the fourth.

decisions.choice: dappled: spotted or speckled
decisions.reason: The word is used of the spotted goats in Jacob's flocks (Genesis 31:10, 12). It describes a horse marked with patches or spots of color.

decisions.choice: strong ones: the horses of the fourth chariot are powerful
alternatives: a color, such as gray or piebald
decisions.reason: The word means strong. It stands after "dappled" with no "and", so it may describe the dappled horses, or all four teams. In verse 7 "the strong ones" are spoken of as if they were a group of their own, and some take the word as another color. The translation reads it as a further description of the fourth team.

decisions.choice: strong, spotted horses (R)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the two descriptions together before the noun and says "spotted" for "dappled". Balanced says "powerful ones".

source.text: וָאַ֨עַן֙ וָֽאֹמַ֔ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י מָה־אֵ֖לֶּה אֲדֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I answered and said to the angel who talks with me, What [are] these, my lord?

en.L: And I answered and said to the angel who talked with me, "What [are] these, my lord?"
en.B: I asked the angel who talked with me, "My lord, what are these?"
en.R: I asked the angel who talked with me, "My lord, what are these?"

decisions.choice: what are these: the question asked in each vision
decisions.reason: Zechariah asks the same question as in 1:9, 2:2 and 4:4. This is the angel's last appearance.

decisions.choice: My lord, what are these? (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording of 4:4 at each level.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַן הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֑י אֵ֗לֶּה אַרְבַּע֙ רֻח֣וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם יוֹצְא֕וֹת מֵֽהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־אֲד֥וֹן כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered the angel and said to me, These [are the] four winds of the heavens, going out from presenting themselves before [the] Lord of all the earth.

en.L: And the angel answered and said to me, "These [are] the four winds of the heavens, going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth.
en.B: The angel answered me, "These are the four winds of heaven, going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth.
en.R: The angel answered, "These are the four winds of heaven. They are going out after standing before the Lord of the whole earth.

decisions.choice: the four winds of heaven: the winds from the four directions, the LORD's servants
decisions.reason: The word means wind or spirit. "The four winds of heaven" are the winds from the four quarters of the world (2:10; Jeremiah 49:36; Daniel 7:2), and Psalm 104:4 says that God makes the winds his messengers. Some read "spirits", heavenly beings, which fits the picture of servants presenting themselves before their Lord. Either way the chariots carry out God's will in every direction.

decisions.choice: presenting themselves before: standing before a king to receive orders
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the heavenly beings who present themselves before the LORD in Job 1:6 and 2:1. Like servants at a royal court, the chariots stand before their Lord and then go out to do what he commands.

decisions.choice: the Lord of all the earth
decisions.reason: The same title as in 4:14.

decisions.choice: the four winds of the heavens (L); of heaven (B, R); Lord, capitalized
decisions.reason: The picture of the winds is kept at every level, as set for the visions. The angel's explanation runs to the end of verse 6, where the quotation mark closes.

source.text: אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֞הּ הַסּוּסִ֣ים הַשְּׁחֹרִ֗ים יֹֽצְאִים֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן וְהַלְּבָנִ֔ים יָצְא֖וּ אֶל־אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְהַ֨בְּרֻדִּ֔ים יָצְא֖וּ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ הַתֵּימָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: [The one] which [has] in it the horses the black [is] going out to [the] land of [the] north, and the white went out after them, and the dappled went out to the land of the south.

en.L: The one with the black horses is going out to the land of the north, and the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south."
en.B: The chariot pulled by the black horses is heading for the land of the north, the white horses have gone out after them, and the dappled horses have gone toward the land of the south."
en.R: The chariot with the black horses is going toward the north. The white horses are following them, and the spotted horses are going toward the south."

decisions.choice: the white went out after them: the white horses follow the black to the north
alternatives: the white went out to the west
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "after them". The word for "behind" can also mean "west" (the Hebrews faced east to name directions), and with a slight change some read "to the west", so that the chariots go to the north, west and south. As the text stands, two chariots go north, toward Babylon, and one south. No chariot is said to go east, and the red horses are not mentioned.

decisions.choice: the land of the north ... the land of the south: Babylon and Egypt
decisions.reason: The north is the direction from which Babylon's armies came and to which Judah was exiled (2:10). The south is the land of Egypt, the other great power. The chariots go out to the lands that had held God's people.

decisions.choice: The chariot (B, R); horses (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the one in which are the black horses" and then names the other teams only by color. Balanced and Readable add "chariot" and "horses" for clarity. The closing mark ends the angel's words begun in verse 5.

source.text: וְהָאֲמֻצִּ֣ים יָצְא֗וּ וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ לְהִתְהַלֵּ֣ךבָּאָ֔רֶץ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְכ֖וּ הִתְהַלְּכ֣וּ בָאָ֑רֶץ וַתִּתְהַלַּ֖כְנָה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the strong went out, and they sought to go, to go about in the earth; and he said, Go, go about in the earth. And they went about in the earth.

en.L: And the strong ones went out, and they sought to go to walk about through the earth; and he said, "Go, walk about through the earth." And they walked about through the earth.
en.B: When the powerful horses came out, they were eager to set off and patrol the earth. He said, "Go, patrol the earth!" So they patrolled the earth.
en.R: When the strong horses came out, they wanted to go and travel all over the earth. He said, "Go and travel all over the earth!" So they went all over the earth.

decisions.choice: walk about through the earth: patrol the earth, as the horsemen did in 1:10-11
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the horsemen of the first vision. The horses strain to go, and are given leave.

decisions.choice: the strong ones: the horses of the fourth chariot, or all the teams; he: the LORD or the angel
decisions.reason: "The strong ones" may be the dappled horses of verse 3 or the whole company of horses. The one who says "Go" is not named; it may be the Lord of all the earth, before whom they stood (verse 5), or the angel speaking for him.

decisions.choice: walk about (L); patrol (B); travel all over (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as in 1:10-11 at each level, so the reader can see the link between the first and the last vision.

source.text: וַיַּזְעֵ֣ק אֹתִ֔י וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר רְאֵ֗ה הַיּֽוֹצְאִים֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן הֵנִ֥יחוּ אֶת־רוּחִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפֽוֹן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, See, those going out to [the] land of [the] north have caused to rest my spirit in [the] land of [the] north.

en.L: And he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, "See, those going out to the land of the north have set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} spirit at rest in the land of the north."
en.B: Then he called out to me, "Look, those going toward the land of the north have given {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} spirit rest in the land of the north."
en.R: Then he called out to me, "Look! The ones going toward the north have calmed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against the land of the north."

decisions.choice: he cried out to me: the speaker voices the LORD
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named, but he says "my spirit", which is the LORD's. Either the LORD himself speaks, or the angel speaks in his name. Either way, the words are the LORD's.

decisions.choice: set my spirit at rest: my anger has been satisfied
alternatives: have placed my Spirit on the land of the north, stirring the exiles to return
decisions.reason: The word for spirit can mean anger or passion (Judges 8:3; Ecclesiastes 10:4), and Ezekiel uses a similar phrase for God's wrath coming to rest after it has done its work (Ezekiel 5:13; 16:42; 24:13). Read that way, the chariots have carried out judgment on Babylon, and the LORD's anger is at rest. Others read it as God's Spirit set on the north, stirring the exiles there to come home (compare Ezra 1:1, 5), which leads well into verse 10. The translation follows the first reading; the Hebrew could carry either.

decisions.choice: rest: the visions end with the LORD's purpose fulfilled
decisions.reason: The first vision found the nations at rest while Jerusalem lay in ruins and the LORD was angry with them (1:11, 15). The last ends with the LORD's own spirit at rest, because his judgment on the north has been carried out.

decisions.choice: spirit, lowercase (L, B); anger (R)
decisions.reason: The word here means God's inner feeling, his anger (m2), not his Spirit as a person, so it is lowercase; Readable says "anger". "My" takes the setting for pronouns of God. Balanced and Readable leave out the repeated "spoke to me, saying".

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: a new message after the visions: a sign with crowns
decisions.reason: The visions are over. The word that follows tells Zechariah to perform a sign: to make a crown from the exiles' gifts and set it on the high priest's head, as a pledge of the Branch who will build the temple (verses 10-15).

decisions.choice: the formula as in 4:8
decisions.reason: The wording set for the prophets, as in 4:8.

source.text: לָק֨וֹחַ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת הַגּוֹלָ֔ה מֵחֶלְדַּ֕י וּמֵאֵ֥ת טוֹבִיָּ֖ה וּמֵאֵ֣ת יְדַֽעְיָ֑ה וּבָאתָ֤ אַתָּה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וּבָ֗אתָ בֵּ֚ית יֹאשִׁיָּ֣ה בֶן־צְפַנְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖אוּ מִבָּבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Take from the exiles, from Heldai and from Tobiah and from Jedaiah, and come you on the day that, and come [to the] house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who have come from Babylon.

en.L: Take from the exiles, from Heldai, from Tobiah and from Jedaiah, and you, go on that same day, go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, they who have come from Babylon.
en.B: Take a gift from the exiles Heldai, Tobiah and Jedaiah, who have just come from Babylon, and on that same day go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
en.R: Heldai, Tobiah and Jedaiah have come back from exile in Babylon. Take a gift from them, and on that same day go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.

decisions.choice: the exiles: Jews still living in Babylon, who sent gifts to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "The exile" is the name for the community of Jews taken to Babylon and their descendants. Many stayed there after the return began, and sent silver and gold for the temple (Ezra 1:4, 6; 7:15-16; 8:25-30). Heldai, Tobiah and Jedaiah seem to have brought such gifts.

decisions.choice: take ... who have come from Babylon: take the silver and gold the three men have brought
alternatives: Josiah's household, who have come from Babylon
decisions.reason: "Take" has no object until verse 11, which names silver and gold. "Who have come" is plural, so it most likely refers to the three men, who may be staying in Josiah's house. It could refer to Josiah's household. The Hebrew joins the clauses loosely; the sense is clear enough.

decisions.choice: a gift (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is to be taken, which verse 11 makes plain. They put "who have arrived from Babylon" next to the three men. Literal keeps the Hebrew order and "you, go".

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ כֶֽסֶף־וְזָהָ֖ב וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ עֲטָר֑וֹת וְשַׂמְתָּ֗ בְּרֹ֛אשׁ יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָ֖ק הַכֹּהֵ֥ן הַגָּדֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take silver and gold, and you will make crowns, and you will set on [the] head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the priest the great.

en.L: And take silver and gold, and make crowns, and set [it] on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
en.B: Take the silver and gold and make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
en.R: Take the silver and gold and make a crown. Put it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.

decisions.choice: crowns: one crown made of several rings, or a crown of silver and one of gold
alternatives: two crowns, one for Joshua and one for the Branch
decisions.reason: The word is plural, but in verse 14 it takes a singular verb ("the crowns will be"), and only one head is named. The plural may mean one splendid crown made of several circlets (compare Revelation 19:12, "many crowns"), or two crowns, of which only one is set on Joshua. The translation reads one crown at the levels that do not keep the Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: Joshua son of Jehozadak: the high priest of chapter 3
decisions.reason: His father Jehozadak was taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar (1 Chronicles 5:41). In Ezra he is called Jeshua son of Jozadak; see the note at Haggai 1:1.

decisions.choice: the crown set on the high priest: a sign pointing to the Branch
decisions.reason: Kings, not priests, wore crowns. Joshua is crowned as a sign, as he and his fellow priests were called "men of a sign" in 3:8, pointing to "a man whose name is the Branch" (verse 12). Because the Branch is a king of David's line, some have suggested that the crown was first meant for Zerubbabel, but no manuscript names him here. The text as it stands joins priest and king in one sign (verse 13).

decisions.choice: crowns (L); a crown (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plural form; Balanced and Readable say "a crown", following the singular verb of verse 14 (m1).

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּה־אִ֞ישׁ צֶ֤מַח שְׁמוֹ֙ וּמִתַּחְתָּ֣יו יִצְמָ֔ח וּבָנָ֖ה אֶת־הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will say to him, saying, Thus says Yahweh of hosts, saying: Look, a man, Branch [is] his name, and from under him he will sprout, and he will build the temple of Yahweh.

en.L: And say to him, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Look, a man whose name [is] the Branch! And from his place he will branch out, and he will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Say to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Here is the man whose name is the Branch. He will branch out from his place, and he will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Tell him, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Here is the man whose name is the Branch. He will grow up from his own place, and he will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a man whose name is the Branch: the coming king promised in 3:8
decisions.reason: See the note at 3:8. "Look, a man" may point to Joshua as the sign, but the Branch is spoken of as another person, who will build the temple and rule (verse 13). Zerubbabel, of David's line, had begun the temple and was to finish it (4:9), and many readers see him here. Jewish tradition read the Branch as the Messiah, and Christians see the promise fulfilled in Jesus. The text names him by his title only.

decisions.choice: from his place he will branch out: a play on his name
decisions.reason: The verb "branch out" or "sprout" comes from the same root as "Branch". "From under him" means from where he stands, from his own roots: he will spring up in the land, not be brought in from outside.

decisions.choice: the temple: the LORD's house, the palace of the divine King
decisions.reason: The word means a palace or great house, and is used for the LORD's temple (Haggai 2:15, 18). The Branch will build it.

decisions.choice: the Branch, capitalized; branch out (L, B); grow up (R); no deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 3:8 and Jeremiah 23:5, "Branch" is capitalized at every level. Literal and Balanced say "branch out" to keep the play on the name; Readable says "grow up". The Branch takes no deity_pronoun setting, as Isaiah's servant does not. The words Zechariah is to say are in double quotation marks and close at the end of verse 13.

source.text: וְ֠הוּא יִבְנֶ֞ה אֶת־הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וְהֽוּא־יִשָּׂ֣א ה֔וֹד וְיָשַׁ֥ב וּמָשַׁ֖ל עַל־כִּסְא֑וֹ וְהָיָ֤ה כֹהֵן֙ עַל־כִּסְא֔וֹ וַעֲצַ֣ת שָׁל֔וֹם תִּהְיֶ֖ה בֵּ֥ין שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will build the temple of Yahweh, and he will bear majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne; and there will be a priest on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them.

en.L: Yes, he will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he will bear majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne; and there will be a priest on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them."
en.B: It is he who will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he will be clothed with majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne. There will be a priest on his throne, and the two of them will be in peaceful agreement."
en.R: He is the one who will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He will be given royal honor, and he will sit on his throne and rule. And there will be a priest on his throne. The two of them will work together in peace."

decisions.choice: he will build: stress on the one who builds
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "he" and the promise of verse 12, to stress that this man, and no other, will build the LORD's temple.

decisions.choice: majesty: royal splendor
decisions.reason: The word is used of the honor and glory of kings (Psalm 21:6; 45:4; Jeremiah 22:18). The Branch will bear it as a king.

decisions.choice: there will be a priest on his throne: a priest will sit on a throne beside the king
alternatives: he will be a priest on his throne (the king himself will also be a priest)
a priest will stand at his right hand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read in two ways. "He will be a priest on his throne" makes the Branch himself both king and priest, and the two in the last clause would be his two offices; this reading is often joined to Psalm 110:4 and to Hebrews 7. Or "there will be a priest on his throne", that is, a priest will sit on a throne of his own, and "the two of them", king and priest, will act in harmony. The Greek translation reads "a priest at his right hand". The translation keeps the Hebrew words so that both readings remain open; the mention of "the two of them" fits the second best.

decisions.choice: a counsel of peace between them: full agreement in their plans
decisions.reason: "Counsel" means plans or purpose. King and priest, or the two offices joined in one man, will act together without rivalry.

decisions.choice: Yes, he (L); It is he who (B); He is the one who (R); be clothed with majesty (B); be given royal honor (R)
decisions.reason: Each level marks the stress of the repeated "he" (m1). Balanced says "be clothed with majesty", a common picture for bearing royal glory, and Readable says what majesty means. The pronouns for the Branch take no deity_pronoun setting.

records.literal_gloss: And the crowns will be for Helem and for Tobiah and for Jedaiah and for Hen son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in [the] temple of Yahweh.

en.L: And the crowns will be for Helem, for Tobiah, for Jedaiah and for Hen son of Zephaniah, as a memorial in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The crown will be kept in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a memorial to Helem, Tobiah, Jedaiah and Hen son of Zephaniah.
en.R: The crown will be kept in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a reminder, in honor of Helem, Tobiah, Jedaiah and Hen son of Zephaniah.

decisions.choice: Helem and Hen: other names for Heldai and Josiah of verse 10
alternatives: Hen as a word: by the kindness of the son of Zephaniah
decisions.reason: Helem seems to be another form of the name Heldai (verse 10). Hen is a word meaning "favor" or "kindness", and stands where Josiah son of Zephaniah stood in verse 10; it may be another name for him, or the phrase may mean "for the kindness of the son of Zephaniah", who received the men in his house. The Syriac translation reads Heldai and Josiah, as in verse 10. This description of the Syriac is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: a memorial: something kept before the LORD as a reminder
decisions.reason: Things kept "as a memorial" in the sanctuary reminded God and the people of something (Exodus 28:12, 29; 30:16; Numbers 31:54). The crown, laid up in the temple, would recall the gift of the exiles and the promise of the Branch until it was fulfilled.

decisions.choice: The crown (B, R); kept in the temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Balanced and Readable read one crown. They add "kept" to make the sense of a memorial "in the temple" plain. Literal keeps the plural.

source.text: וּרְחוֹקִ֣ים׀יָבֹ֗אוּ וּבָנוּ֙ בְּהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָיָה֙ אִם־שָׁמ֣וֹעַ תִּשְׁמְע֔וּן בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And [those] far off will come and build in [the] temple of Yahweh, and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me to you. And it will be, if diligently you will listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God.

en.L: And those who are far off will come and build in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me to you. And [this] will come about, if you will diligently listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.
en.B: People who are far away will come and help build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you. All this will come about if you carefully obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.
en.R: People from far away will come and help build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you. All this will happen if you really obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: those who are far off: Jews still in distant lands, and perhaps the nations
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the exiles still scattered abroad, like the men who brought gifts from Babylon (verse 10), or foreigners who will come to the LORD (2:15; 8:20-22; Isaiah 60:10). Either way, help for the temple will come from far away.

decisions.choice: if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God: the condition of Deuteronomy 28:1
decisions.reason: The words are those of Deuteronomy 28:1, where the blessings of the covenant depend on obedience. The sentence breaks off after "if", leaving the hearer to supply the blessing. The promises are sure, but the people's share in them depends on their obedience.

decisions.choice: you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me: the proof of the prophet's word
decisions.reason: The same assurance as in 2:13, 2:15 and 4:9.

decisions.choice: carefully obey (B); really obey (R)
alternatives: diligently listen to the voice of
decisions.reason: "Listen to the voice" means to obey, so Balanced and Readable say "obey", and add a word for the strengthening of the verb. Literal says "you shall know", as in 2:13.
